questions.title: With which country will the United States record its largest trade deficit in May 2026?
questions.background: The United States publishes monthly trade data, including trade balances with its major trading partners.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve using the country-level trade balances in the initial May 2026 trade report from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau. Identify the individual country associated with the largest U.S. trade deficit, excluding regional groupings. Resolution Date : 2026-07-07 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: The June 26 Census Bureau Advance Economic Indicators report for May 2026 revealed a massive surprise blowout in the seasonally adjusted U.S. goods trade deficit from $83.01B in April to $105.75B in May (+$22.74B vs. $85B consensus), driven by both a +$10.90B (+3.6% m/m) import jump to $313.43B and an -$11.84B (-5.4% m/m) plunge in U.S. goods exports. Crucially, the end-use import breakdown cuts against Taiwan's runaway lead: capital goods ex-autos (Taiwan's core AI server/chip mix) rose only +0.4% m/m (slowest of all six categories), whereas nonfood consumer goods ex-autos (Vietnam and China) surged +5.7% m/m, automotive vehicles & parts (Mexico) jumped +6.3% m/m, and foods/beverages (Mexico) rose +4.3% m/m. Because Taiwan and Vietnam were tied at $19.3B in April Exhibit 19, while Mexico ($14.8B) and China ($12.0B) benefit both from surging consumer/auto imports and any share of the -$11.8B U.S. export drop (with China's customs U.S. surplus also rebounding +$2.95B), trimming Taiwan from 0.52 to 0.43, lifting Vietnam (0.35 -> 0.37), Mexico (0.06 -> 0.10), China (0.06 -> 0.07), and a 3% tail for a surprise gold/pharma swing (Switzerland/Ireland) ahead of the July 7 FT-900 release.

questions.title: Which UK party leader will announce plans in early July 2026 to resign as an MP and contest the resulting by-election?
questions.background: A parliamentary resignation can trigger a by-election, which the departing MP may contest to seek a fresh mandate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public announcements corroborated by contemporaneous reporting from BBC News, The Guardian, or Al Jazeera. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the UK political party leader who publicly announces, between July 1 and July 9, 2026, plans to resign from the House of Commons and stand in the by-election caused by that resignation. The announcement is sufficient; the by-election need not have taken place. Accepted Answer Format : The party leader's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Rupert Lowe (Restore Britain leader, MP for Great Yarmouth) uniquely fits both historical UK precedents for an MP resigning to contest a by-election: he was elected under Reform UK in 2024 before launching Restore Britain in Feb 2026 (which just finished 3rd in Makerfield with ~7%), and on May 15, 2026 he lost his High Court challenge to halt a parliamentary ICGS watchdog probe, creating strong incentive to seek a fresh mandate or preempt a suspension/recall petition. Very few UK party leaders sit in the Commons; Nigel Farage (Reform UK), Jeremy Corbyn (Your Party, elected Independent), Zarah Sultana (ex-Labour/Your Party), and Kemi Badenoch represent smaller tails, with ~12% left for other minor-party MP leaders (e.g., Northern Ireland party leaders or a newly formed breakaway party).

questions.background: Alexandru Munteanu has resigned as Moldova’s prime minister, triggering his cabinet’s resignation. Moldova is pursuing European Union membership.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Moldovan parliamentary announcements or reliable news reporting confirming the election of a new prime minister. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first person elected prime minister by Moldova’s parliament following Alexandru Munteanu’s resignation. A nomination or temporary appointment as acting prime minister does not qualify. Resolution Date : The date parliament elects the successor. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the person elected.
questions.current_reasoning: Targeted Moldovan Romanian-language search (TVR Moldova, UNIMEDIA, Politics.md, Logos Press, Moldpres, July 3-4) reveals new insider context behind PM Alexandru Munteanu's July 3 resignation: President Maia Sandu disclosed that Munteanu's sole objection was a personal clash with Education and Research Minister and PAS VP Dan Perciun following a Tuesday dispute over fiscal/budget policy (the exact policy Sandu now says the next cabinet must rethink). Perciun was spotted at the Presidency Friday morning right after the resignation and was the only cabinet figure journalists pressed Sandu about as a rumored PM successor; while Perciun publicly denied candidacy ('I want to continue at Education') and Sandu refused to name candidates ahead of next week's constitutional faction consultations (with Munteanu staying interim PM and opposition Democrația Acasă vowing to propose its own nominee), standard pre-consultation denials and Perciun's senior PAS profile warrant adding Dan Perciun into the top 5 at 0.12 while dropping scandal-adjacent Vladimir Bolea (linked to Infrastructure/MoldATSA and formerly Agriculture). Retaining Mihai Popșoi (0.16), Cristina Gherasimov (0.15), Igor Grosu (0.12, framing PAS steps from Parliament), and Eugen Osmochescu (0.06), leaving 39% for other PAS insiders, former PMs, or another unexpected Sandu technocrat.

questions.title: What principal criminal penalty will Hannah Dugan receive at her initial sentencing for obstructing a federal proceeding?
questions.background: A federal jury convicted Wisconsin judge Hannah Dugan of obstructing a federal proceeding in December 2025. The case concerned her response to immigration agents seeking to arrest a defendant at her courthouse.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The federal court’s sentencing judgment or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the sentence announced in court. Resolution Conditions : Resolve when the federal district court first imposes a sentence for Dugan’s obstruction conviction. Identify the principal criminal penalty imposed at that sentencing. Subsequent appeals or resentencing do not change the answer. Accepted Answer Format : A short noun phrase naming the principal criminal penalty.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 1-2 court filings overhaul the sentencing outlook ahead of former Milwaukee County Judge Hannah Dugan's July 8 sentencing before U.S. District Judge Lynn Adelman (reported by Bloomberg Law, WTMJ, TMJ4, and USA Today Network). First, contrary to prior assumptions that guidelines recommended probation, the federal presentence report actually calculates a Zone D guideline range of 15 to 21 months in prison, and prosecutors cited the 16-month national obstruction average, Dugan's violation of her judicial oath, and her lack of remorse—asking for a 'serious' and 'meaningful' sentence (though notably declining to demand a specific month figure). Second, Dugan's defense formally requested a sentence of 'time served' (she spent part of a day in federal custody), arguing overcharging (0-6 months range), decades of public service, ~20 letters of support (including former DA E. Michael McCann and Judge Joe Wall), and severe collateral consequences. While liberal Judge Adelman frequently varies downward below guidelines, the 15-21 month guideline anchor and lack of remorse sharply raise Prison sentence (0.18 -> 0.30, mainly via a short below-guidelines term), while the defense's explicit ask vaults Time served from 0.02 to 0.19. Probation drops from an overconfident 0.66 to 0.40, still plural favorite as Judge Adelman's classic non-custodial compromise that imposes formal felony accountability defensible on 7th Circuit review, with Home confinement steady at 0.07 and Fine trimmed to 0.02 (2% residual for community service or other phrasing).

questions.background: Alibaba's 2014 US initial public offering raised $25 billion, setting the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign company.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official issuer announcements and contemporaneous reporting by reputable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the company reported as holding the all-time record for the largest US initial public offering by a foreign company as of July 10, 2026. Compare offerings by proceeds raised, not company valuation. An offering whose pricing and share sales have been announced may qualify before exchange trading begins. Accepted Answer Format : The company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: A sharp July 3 rebound in Seoul restored SK Hynix's valuation buffer above Alibaba's $25.0B record right ahead of Monday July 6 bookbuilding and July 9 pricing. After plunging 14.57% to 2,187,000 KRW on July 2 (leaving $25.01B gross value and zero buffer), SK Hynix rallied +10.88% on July 3 to close at 2,425,000 KRW as KOSPI snapped back +5.76% to 8,088.34 (triggering a buy-side sidecar on 4.46T won of net institutional buying), while the won strengthened 30.2 won to 1,525.6/USD after weak US June payrolls dimmed Fed rate-hike bets. At Friday's Seoul close (with US markets closed July 3 and KOSPI closed for the weekend), the 17.79M board-authorized new shares equal 43.14T KRW or $28.28B gross (+13.1% in USD overnight), generating $26.86B at a 5% ADR discount and clearing $25.03B at any discount up to 11.5%. July 3 Korea Herald reiterates the July 10 Nasdaq debut targeting up to $30B, and Aju Press confirms the Form F-1/A kept the July 6-9 calendar intact. Reversing back to SK Hynix 0.61 / Alibaba 0.39, leaving substantial Alibaba mass given extreme realized volatility, an 11th straight session of foreign net KOSPI selling (2.19T won July 3), ADR pricing discount/downsizing risk, and residual delay risk before July 9 pricing (with Samsung's July 7 preliminary Q2 earnings as the next major catalyst).

questions.title: Which team will win the England–India T20 international series in July 2026?
questions.background: India and England are scheduled to contest a T20 international series in England.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match results or contemporaneous AFP reporting identifying the winner of the England–India T20 international series in July 2026. Resolution Timing : Resolve when a team secures an unassailable series lead, or when the series concludes if its winner has not previously been determined. Accepted Answer Format : The country name of the series-winning team.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 4 series shift (Reuters, Hindustan Times): England defeated India by 4 wickets with an over to spare in the 2nd T20I at Old Trafford—chasing 191 behind Jacob Bethell's unbeaten 76 off 46 (including a 29-run 17th over off Ravi Bishnoi, 0/60) and Harry Brook's 39 off 15 after Sam Curran's 3/33—to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series with only three matches remaining (July 7 Trent Bridge, July 9 Bristol, July 11 Southampton) following the July 1 Durham rain washout. Starting from 1-0 with three games left heavily tilts decisive series outcomes toward England: with no further rainouts, England win the series outright with 2 of 3 (4-0 or 3-1), whereas India must sweep all three remaining games (3-0) to win 3-1; with one further rainout, England need just 1 of 2 while India must still win both. India showed real competitiveness (190/7 with Kishan 49, Abhishek 43, Sooryavanshi 14 on debut; Arshdeep 3 wkts, Axar 1/20; on top after 16 overs before Bishnoi's two no-balls), keeping true per-match odds close (~53% England at home, consistent with pre-match 52.6% Racing Post pricing). Conditional on a decisive series winner (Accepted Answer Format requires the country name of the series-winning team), integrating over per-match strength uncertainty (sd=0.06) and UK rainout risk (5-20% per match) shifts England sharply up from 0.55 to 0.82 and India down from 0.45 to 0.18.

questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major northward shift in July 4 Taiwanese and European meteorological guidance sharply boosts Zhejiang and trims Fujian and Guangdong. CMA upgraded Bavi to Super Typhoon (60 m/s, 920 hPa, 300-380 km gale radius) on July 4 morning (JTWC 269 km/h Cat 5 approaching Rota/Marianas Monday July 6), projecting no impact on China's waters before July 8 and closest approach to Taiwan on July 10-11 with a massive 350 km gale radius. Crucially, July 4 briefings from CWA forecaster Zheng Jieren (CNA, NOWnews) and meteorologist Jia Xinxing (ETtoday, TVBS, FTVNews) reverse much of July 3's southward GFS/ECMWF swing: ECMWF's deterministic run shifted north to grazing northern Taiwan or passing west of Miyako Island; ECMWF's traditional ensemble now gives only 30-40% probability of Taiwan landfall (>60% no Taiwan landfall); ECMWF AI (AIFS) projects passage near Miyako Island with <20% chance of heading toward Taiwan; and CWA states passing over the ocean east/NE of Taiwan is more likely. Under the dominant July 4 track (waters off northern Taiwan / west of Miyako Island entering the East China Sea on July 10-11), Zhejiang (Wenzhou, Taizhou, Ningbo, Zhoushan) overwhelmingly leads pre-emptive evacuations by July 11 (~75-80%, plus ~38% share even on northern Taiwan landfall and ~70% on Okinawa/East China Sea offshore tracks). Blending our 4-regime model while retaining prudent 6-day subtropical-ridge uncertainty (~200 km forecast error noted by Jia Xinxing) lifts Zhejiang +0.110 (0.45 -> 0.56), lowers Fujian -0.070 (0.35 -> 0.28), cuts Guangdong -0.050 (0.11 -> 0.06 as Bashi Channel scenarios recede), and nudges Shanghai (0.04 -> 0.055) and Jiangsu (0.02 -> 0.025) higher on northern East China Sea approaches, leaving 0.020 tail.

questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Notable northward track shift on July 4 pulls Zhejiang into a virtual dead heat with Fujian and cuts Guangdong roughly in half. July 4 updates from CWA (CNA, NOWnews) and Jia Xinxing (ETtoday, TVBS, FTVNews) show ECMWF deterministic shifting north toward the waters off northern Taiwan / west of Miyako Island, ECMWF's traditional ensemble cutting Taiwan-landfall probability to 30-40% (>60% offshore), and ECMWF AI targeting Miyako Island (<20% Taiwan landfall), while Bashi Channel tracks have largely faded from official briefings. Because this question is strictly conditional on a qualifying mainland China landfall (void if Bavi recurves cleanly into Japan/Korea), Bayes' rule still weights the ~25-30% northern-Taiwan-landfall regime (~88% mainland landfall -> ~66% Fujian / ~31% Zhejiang) and ~8-10% residual southern/Bashi tail (~92% mainland landfall -> ~48% Fujian / ~46% Guangdong) heavily alongside the surging ~42-45% north-of-Taiwan/west-of-Miyako regime (~55% mainland landfall -> ~58% Zhejiang / ~20% Fujian / ~10% Shanghai / ~7% Jiangsu). Consequently, conditional on mainland China landfall, Zhejiang surges +0.080 (0.315 -> 0.395) to nearly tie Fujian (0.465 -> 0.405, -0.060), Guangdong drops -0.065 (0.145 -> 0.080, keeping a realistic 6-day ridge-uncertainty tail), and Shanghai (0.030 -> 0.055) and Jiangsu (0.025 -> 0.035) rise on East China Sea NW-curve scenarios, leaving 0.030 for Shandong/Liaoning/Hainan/Guangxi.

questions.title: Which UK university will be identified in nationwide reporting by the end of July 2026 as having investigated the most students for pro-Palestine activism between October 2023 and November 2025?
questions.background: Pro-Palestinian campus protests in Britain have prompted disputes over university disciplinary practices and freedom of expression.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Nationwide comparative reporting by Al Jazeera and Liberty Investigates, drawing on university Freedom of Information disclosures and available by July 31, 2026. Resolution Rule : Resolve to the university with the highest reported number of students subjected to disciplinary investigations for pro-Palestine activism between October 2023 and November 2025 among the universities covered. Investigations need not have resulted in sanctions. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the university.
questions.current_reasoning: Al Jazeera English and Liberty Investigates already launched their 2026 FOI series (to >150 UK universities) in April 2026; in Liberty Investigates' earlier Feb 2025 FOI dataset covering Oct 2023-Aug 2024, University College London led all known UK institutions with 12 students investigated (ahead of Cardiff with 9 by April 2025, King's College London with 7, and LSE with at least 7). UCL also has one of the UK's largest student bodies and a proven track record of disclosing exact student counts rather than redacting under personal-data exemptions. Extending the window through Nov 2025 brings large protest-heavy campuses like Manchester and Oxford (both featured in the April 2026 Al Jazeera/Liberty Investigates Horus surveillance disclosures) into contention, while 40% mass remains across the broad field of other UK universities (SOAS, LSE, Edinburgh, Cambridge, Sheffield, Queen Mary, Leeds, Warwick, Bristol, etc.).
